title: Cancellation, recovery, and exactly-one publication
boundary_reason: Terminal arbitration crosses durable control, process cleanup, immutable evidence, canonical apply compensation, publication, and flow projection.
behavioral_concerns: Cancellation must stop new work, propagate to active process trees, reserve cleanup time, and produce a distinct inspectable outcome.
Interrupted apply may restore only digest-bound known preimages; unknown bytes, links, missing records, or identity drift must produce cleanup uncertainty.
Late runtime completion and stale fencing generations must not overwrite a terminal result.
Recovery must be idempotent, runtime-free, deadline-preserving, and unable to infer a pass.

evidence.summary: Bounded source inspection found multiple ignored isolation.cleanup results in optimization rejection paths, some immediately followed by continue.

attempts.stop_reason: verification_unavailable: The sole approved path is in package internal/app, but the required failure occurs inside unexported internal/sprint optimizePerformance and performanceIsolation cleanup logic. The public orchestration API has no deterministic isolation cleanup injection seam. Reaching the branch from app would require filesystem sabotage of product-created temporary directories, which cannot reliably distinguish cleanup failure from infrastructure behavior and therefore would violate the frozen inconclusive conditions. Source matching and independent simulation were explicitly rejected.. Required prerequisite: Approve an internal/sprint/*_test.go path in package sprint, where optimizePerformance and performanceIsolation can be exercised directly, or expose an existing product-owned deterministic isolation/cleanup test hook through sprint.Service.

theories.claim: Optimization paths discard isolation cleanup failures and may continue into another mutation cycle instead of publishing cleanup_uncertain and stopping new work.
theories.basis: The optimization implementation repeatedly ignores isolation.cleanup() results before continuing or returning unrelated errors, despite the cleanup and cancellation requirements (qa-v1-block-af5f117594728fd0aab939e2, qa-v1-block-3bf230d4d7d4d3f748ebe877, qa-v1-block-1bec30a6414976c9c25b5d55, qa-v1-block-ce45392d2ebc036986b89d13, qa-v1-block-5bfa81fcf97f6db90cfa9405).
theories.verification_surface: internal/sprint/performance_optimize_runtime.go cleanup handling after rejected or invalid optimization proposals
theories.confirmation_condition: A branch calls isolation.cleanup(), ignores a non-nil result, and continues or returns an error that does not preserve cleanup uncertainty, allowing later work or an incorrect terminal outcome.
theories.refutation_condition: Every isolation cleanup result is checked and any incomplete cleanup immediately prevents further work and is propagated so the durable result becomes cleanup_uncertain.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The cited source does not expose cleanup handling for optimization rejection and continuation branches.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Statically inspect bounded optimization cleanup branches and trace returned errors through RunPerformance and finishPerformanceFailure; no runtime or mutation is needed.
